title: Checking the Eye Pressure, Carefully

patient.name: Mr Rajendran s/o Muthu
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up visit — monitoring of intraocular pressure, glaucoma suspect

history.hpc: Mr Rajendran was flagged as a glaucoma suspect 6 months ago after a routine optometrist visit found IOP of 24 mmHg in both eyes and a slightly enlarged optic disc cupping. He was referred to SNEC for further assessment and is currently not on any eye drops, pending the results of monitoring visits including today's IOP check. He has no visual symptoms. He reports he had a strong cup of coffee about 30 minutes before arriving today.
history.pmhx: Glaucoma suspect, under monitoring. No previous eye surgery. Mild myopia, wears glasses for distance.
history.family_hx: Elder brother on glaucoma eye drops
history.social_hx: Warehouse supervisor. Non-smoker. Drinks coffee daily.

examination_findings.fundus: C:D ratio 0.6 right, 0.65 left (per prior doctor's notes) — under monitoring

nct_iop.method: Non-contact tonometry (air puff), 3 readings per eye averaged
nct_iop.result: IOP elevated bilaterally, consistent with previous visits — for doctor's review and trend comparison

investigations.iop_trend_note: Previous visit IOP: RE 24 mmHg, LE 25 mmHg (taken at 9:00am) — today's readings broadly consistent

diagnosis: NCT performed correctly with multiple readings averaged for both eyes. IOP remains elevated bilaterally (23-24 mmHg), consistent with prior visits. Findings to be reviewed by doctor alongside disc assessment and visual field results to determine if treatment should be initiated.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm both eyes are to be tested
Perform hand hygiene and wipe all machine parts that contact the patient with alcohol wipes before starting
Ask patient to remove glasses or contact lenses before the test
Position patient comfortably at the NCT machine with chin on chinrest and forehead against the rest
Inform patient that a small puff of air will be blown into each eye and ask him to keep both eyes open and look straight ahead at the target without blinking
Perform NCT on the right eye first by convention, then the left eye, taking at least 3 readings per eye
Check that readings are consistent (not widely scattered) — repeat if there is excessive variability
Note the time of measurement, as IOP fluctuates throughout the day (diurnal variation)
Wipe machine contact parts with alcohol wipes after the procedure and perform hand hygiene
Document RE and LE readings (all values and average) with time of measurement, and compare with previous visit's IOP and time
follow_up: Doctor to review IOP trend alongside optic disc findings and any visual field results
If IOP remains persistently elevated with disc changes, doctor may consider starting IOP-lowering treatment
Patient may be scheduled for HVF or further glaucoma work-up if not already done
patient_education: Explain that the air puff may feel like a quick tickle but is not painful
Explain that eye pressure can vary throughout the day and with factors like caffeine, so results are interpreted alongside other tests
Advise patient to keep his follow-up appointments for monitoring, as early glaucoma often has no symptoms

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms both eyes are to be tested
Asks patient to remove glasses or contact lenses before NCT
Notes contextual factors that can transiently affect IOP, such as recent caffeine intake
Reviews prior IOP readings and the time they were taken for trend comparison (diurnal variation)
Performs hand hygiene and wipes machine contact parts with alcohol wipes before and after
Positions patient correctly and gives clear instructions (look at target, do not blink, do not flinch from air puff)
Takes at least 3 readings per eye and checks for consistency, repeating if widely variable
Documents the time of measurement alongside the IOP values for both eyes
Recognises IOP of 23-24 mmHg is above the normal range (10-21 mmHg) and consistent with glaucoma suspect status
Understands that IOP fluctuates diurnally and with factors such as caffeine, and documents the time of testing accordingly
Does not start or recommend treatment independently — refers trend data to doctor
Identifies the need to compare today's readings with previous visit readings
Documents all IOP readings (individual values, average, time) accurately for both eyes
Flags the IOP trend to the doctor for correlation with disc and field findings
Educates patient on the painless nature of NCT and the importance of follow-up monitoring
Maintains correct infection control practices throughout
